name: Life and Death
_what: Info film for the Life and Death domain: the Rootkin, the Ashwardens and the Threnodists, their homes, crafts, schools, costs and a few public figures, with the Deepwood's Moot and the Afterlings at the edges. Every string in lines/after/name/title is player-facing.

lines: Life and Death. Three peoples live here: one tends growth, one tends endings, one tends grief.
The Quickwood and the Palelands are one Reach, and should balance. Something is pulling it toward the Pale.
The Heartroot was grown, over four hundred years. Its first planters are still alive, and call it a promising start.
The Rootkin's craft is life at flood. Growth is a force, and a Rootkin can point it.
The further they go, the more it pulls them toward life.
In the Slow Orchard trees take a human lifetime to fruit. The Rootkin explain themselves by walking you through it and saying nothing.
Thessa Root planted a tree here three hundred years ago, for someone who has not come.
after: She means to be there when it fruits.

lines: The Greenward is their one concession to urgency: a wall of thorn, grown by people who would rather not have needed it.
The Quickeners bring land back. The Grafters regrow what was lost. The Bloom-Wrights force growth on bodies that did not ask.
Past the Eaves lies the Deepwood. Its Moot is arguing whether to seal the wood from humankind, and the Rootbound are gaining ground.
Thren, Walker of the Thin Edge, argues to keep the wood woven into the world. He knows exactly how the argument is losing.
A Rootkin refuses a death. An Ashwarden attends one.
after: Both are sometimes the mercy. The one doing it does not always get to know which.

lines: At Greypool the two share a roof and a rota. Nobody there is hurried toward an ending, or held back from one.
Cairnhold is the least frightening place in the world once you are inside it.
after: Every house has a second door, toward the fields. The dead leave by it.

lines: The Ashwardens hold that someone has to be competent at the end of things. They ask the dead what they knew, and ease endings already begun.
after: They can draw a life down, too. What goes all the way down does not recover.

lines: Neth has buried more than she has known. She comes to deaths nobody sent for, and has never once looked away.
When she is in the doorway, the dying are not afraid.
shots._why_20261007: P1: an epic, resolved through the legends roster. Lines from EXESA VI and her signature.

lines: Warden-Mother Redgate calls death the end of the road, and means nothing sad by it.
after: She wants no one reaped who was not ready.

lines: The Grave-Callers raise the dead to work, and do not ask first. Half the tradition calls it obscene. The other half has done it for four hundred years.
Past the last cairn the tending stops. The ones who go out into the Long Grey tend to keep going.
after: Reapers work out there. They end what is ready, and have stopped asking what that means.

lines: Some of the dead stay. Orsolya refused her own ending, and has stood at the Last Cairn for forty years, still having the argument.
after: Behind her grew Cairnsend, for the dead who would not lie down.

lines: The Threnodists hold that feeling is the only true knowing. In Wellspring nobody feels anything privately.
Visitors weep within a day, or flee.
At Grief House strangers sit with your loss for as long as it takes. It has never turned anyone away.
The Carriers hold grief for others. The Lament gives a people's mourning its shape.
after: The singer carries what she moves, for as long as it stays moved.

lines: Maud sings the death of anyone who will die within the week, and cannot stop herself.
after: She wants, once, to sing for someone who lives through it.

lines: In the Wellspring Deep are the Raw, who turned feeling past all judgment. Near them you feel things that are not yours, and cannot tell.
At the Hollowing the grey runs out toward a green nobody there has walked to.
after: The road to the Greenward takes most of a year. Every Warden has met someone who made it.
